sections.html:
Up on Crowley's Ridge in the northeast corner of the state, Jonesboro splits the Craighead County seat duties with Lake City. By land area, at about 80.7 square miles, it is the second-biggest city in Arkansas. The 2025 estimate is 83,296 residents, up from 78,576 in 2020 and 55,515 in 2000, and the metro area holds about 139,440 people.

Growth means new subdivisions on the edges while the oldest houses sit near downtown, so a seller in an older part of town competes with newer construction. The city limits contain six public school districts: Jonesboro, Valley View, Nettleton, Westside Consolidated, Bay and Brookland. Your house could be zoned to any of them, so look up the address before you quote a school to a buyer.

Work here centers on Arkansas State University, the biggest single employer, along with health care, agriculture, retail and manufacturing. St. Bernards Regional Medical Center and NEA Baptist both operate here, and the region treats Jonesboro as its hospital hub. The A-State campus, including the NYIT College of Osteopathic Medicine, brings students and staff who rent or buy nearby. Steady university and hospital jobs support a deep pool of renters, which helps a landlord who is weighing a sale.

A landlord can also sell with the tenants in place. Tell a buyer about the lease and rent early, since an occupied house changes what the buyer can do.

Jonesboro has a humid subtropical climate and a record of damaging tornadoes. An F4 tornado on May 15 to 16, 1968, destroyed 164 homes. Another F4 struck on May 27, 1973. On March 28, 2020, an EF3 tornado with peak winds around 140 mph hit the south and east sides of town, damaging homes, airport hangars and The Mall at Turtle Creek.

Buyers here ask about roof age, storm shelters, insurance claims and permit records. If your house was repaired after the 2020 storm, gather the contractor paperwork before you list or accept an offer. Annual precipitation runs about 52 inches, so roofs and drainage get a close look either way.

Jonesboro's code enforcement office uses neighborhood sweeps and a boarding and securing ordinance to push owners to fix blighted property. Sweeps target tall grass, inoperative vehicles, unsanitary conditions and unlawful storage. Officers give a warning first and issue a court citation on a second pass if the problem remains.

The boarding ordinance applies to a vacant building with no utilities connected for 60 days. Broken doors and windows must be secured within seven days, and the owner must repair, rehabilitate or demolish within six months of notice. Fines start at $100 per day, and failure to act can lead to abatement, condemnation or a citation. Code enforcement answers at 870-933-4658.

An empty inherited house is the most common way a seller ends up under this ordinance. Selling before the six months run out moves the repair burden to the buyer.

sections.h2: If you inherited a vacant house
sections.html:
An empty house is where Jonesboro owners most often run into trouble. Utilities get shut off, the grass grows, and the 60-day clock in the boarding ordinance starts without anyone noticing. If you are settling an estate, do these things first:

  • Confirm who has legal authority to sign the deed.
  • Keep the doors and windows secured so no violation can start.
  • Ask the collector for the tax balance and the title company for any liens.
  • Call code enforcement at 870-933-4658 if you already received a notice.

A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can close before the six-month window ends, which spares you the cost of the repairs the notice would demand.

Jonesboro is crossed by AR 1, AR 18, US 49, US 63, US 78 and Interstate 555. Jonesboro Economical Transit (GOJO) runs four fixed bus routes plus paratransit, and Greyhound provides intercity service. The Jonesboro Municipal Airport has commercial service through the federal Essential Air Service program. Crowley's Ridge Parkway, Arkansas's first National Scenic Byway, passes through town.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
The Craighead County Collector takes payment from the first business day of March through October 15 of the year after assessment. Tax unpaid after October 15 carries a 10 percent penalty, and interest on delinquent real estate tax accrues daily. A check in the mail is on time if the postmark is October 15 or earlier.

Collector officeAddress and phone
Jonesboro511 Union Street, Suite 107, 72401; (870) 933-4560
Lake City107 Cobean

Arkansas reappraises real property on four-year cycles under Act 139 of 2023, and a homestead's taxable value can rise only 5 percent a year. To contest a valuation formally, schedule a hearing with the county board of equalization by the third Monday in August. The state's real property transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration, and the deed is recorded at the county clerk.

You can still sell with delinquent tax. The balance is deducted from your sale proceeds by the title company, so get the collector's payoff figure first. Interest accrues daily, so the number changes from week to week.

Once you accept an offer, the title company searches ownership and liens and prepares the settlement statement. That statement shows any tax payoff, the mortgage balance, the transfer tax and your net proceeds. The deed is then recorded with the county clerk. A cash sale has no lender appraisal or loan approval to wait for, so the closing date mostly depends on the title work. A listing adds showings, financing and an appraisal on top of that.

Bring the deed, a photo ID, your latest tax statement and any storm-repair paperwork. A tenant's lease and the current rent belong in the folder too if the house is a rental.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Jonesboro house
sections.html:
Sellers choose among a listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer. An updated house and a flexible calendar favor a listing, though lender financing, inspections and appraisals can stretch the timeline by weeks. A cash deal closes when you say it will.

  • Storm-repaired or older houses: an as-is purchase removes the repair negotiation.
  • Vacant property: selling lets you avoid ongoing code citations.
  • Rental with tenants: ask whether the buyer will keep the lease.
  • Delinquent taxes: request a payoff figure from the collector first.

faqs.q: How many people live in Jonesboro, Arkansas?
faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 83,296 residents, which makes Jonesboro the fifth-largest city in Arkansas.

faqs.q: Is Jonesboro in a tornado-prone area?
faqs.a: Yes. The city has had F4 tornadoes in 1968 and 1973 and an EF3 tornado on March 28, 2020. Buyers often ask about roof age and storm repairs.

faqs.q: When are Craighead County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By October 15 of the year after assessment. After that date a 10 percent penalty applies, and interest on delinquent real estate tax accrues daily.

faqs.q: Can I sell a vacant, damaged house in Jonesboro?
faqs.a: Yes. A building with no utilities for 60 days can trigger the city's boarding and securing rules, so many owners sell before the six-month repair window ends.

faqs.q: What is the Arkansas real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on deeds that convey real property for more than $100.
